skill.name: software-architecture
skill.description: Document software architecture with ARCHITECTURE.md, component docs, and Mermaid diagrams. Use it to map entry points, data flows, component relationships, and key abstractions.
skill.summary: Create and maintain architecture documentation with Mermaid diagrams and component guides.
skill.author: Chemiseblanc

security_audit.summary: All static findings were adjudicated as false positives after reviewing the cited files. The external command alerts are Markdown backticks around paths and examples, and the blocker alerts are Mermaid or documentation language. No prompt injection, data exfiltration, network access, or executable automation was found.

static_findings.snippet: Key test fixtures and utilities: `tests/conftest.py` or equivalent.
Document system architecture using a root `ARCHITECTURE.md` with detailed component docs in `docs/*.
1. **Before major changes**: Read `ARCHITECTURE.md` to understand system structure
3. **When adding components**: Create new `docs/*.md` file and link from `ARCHITECTURE.md`
- Link to detail docs (create `docs/` section even if empty initially)
- One file per logical component in `docs/`
| C4 Context | `ARCHITECTURE.md` - system boundaries and external actors |
| C4 Component | `docs/*.md` - internal structure of a component |
| New component added | Create `docs/<component>.md`, add link to `ARCHITECTURE.md` |
description: Document software architecture using ARCHITECTURE.md and docs/*.md files with Mermaid d

content.value_statement: Architecture knowledge often lives only in code and loses context during refactors. This skill creates concise architecture docs, diagrams, and component references for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code workflows.
actual_capabilities: Creates a root ARCHITECTURE.md with overview, system diagrams, entry points, abstractions, and testing notes.
Creates component detail docs under docs/*.md for major modules and responsibilities.
Selects Mermaid diagram types, including C4, flowchart, sequence, ER, and class diagrams.
Builds entry point and abstraction tables with relative file paths.
Guides documentation updates after components, dependencies, refactors, or entry points change.
limitations: It depends on the repository content available to the AI assistant.
It does not run architecture discovery tools or validate diagrams automatically.
It can miss runtime behavior that is not visible in source files.
It requires human review before publishing architecture decisions as authoritative.

use_cases.title: Create Baseline Architecture Docs
use_cases.description: Generate a first ARCHITECTURE.md for a repository that has code but little design documentation.

use_cases.title: Explain a Complex Component
use_cases.description: Create a focused docs/*.md page for a component with several files, dependencies, and request flows.

use_cases.title: Refresh Docs After Refactoring
use_cases.description: Update diagrams, entry point tables, and component links after structure or dependencies change.

prompt_templates.title: Create Initial Docs
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a repository without architecture documentation.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an ARCHITECTURE.md for this repository. Identify entry points, major components, key abstractions, testing locations, and useful Mermaid diagrams.

prompt_templates.title: Document One Component
prompt_templates.scenario: Focused component documentation for a known area.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a docs page for the authentication component. Include purpose, key files, abstractions, dependencies, data flow, and testing notes.

prompt_templates.title: Update After Refactor
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the recent refactor and update ARCHITECTURE.md plus affected docs/*.md pages. Keep diagrams and file references current.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Documentation Coverage
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit the current architecture docs against the repository. Identify missing components, stale diagrams, weak abstractions, and unclear entry points.

output_examples.input: A service has no architecture docs and several API, worker, and database modules.
output_examples.output: A root architecture overview with a system diagram, entry point table, component list, testing summary, and links for detail docs.

output_examples.input: A data pipeline component has parsing, validation, storage, and export logic spread across files.
output_examples.output: A component guide describing responsibilities, key files, abstractions, dependencies, sequence flow, configuration, and tests.

output_examples.input: A refactor moved the CLI and split core services into smaller modules.
output_examples.output: Updated architecture notes with corrected entry points, revised component relationships, and refreshed maintenance checklist items.

best_practices: Start diagrams with three to five nodes, then add detail only when it improves clarity.
Use relative file paths so readers can navigate from documentation to source quickly.
Update architecture docs in the same change set as structural code changes.
anti_patterns: Do not document every file when a component summary is clearer.
Do not add complex diagrams without explaining the design decision they support.
Do not leave ARCHITECTURE.md disconnected from detailed component docs.

faq.question: What files does this skill create?
faq.answer: It creates or updates ARCHITECTURE.md and optional docs/*.md component pages.

faq.question: Does it use Mermaid diagrams?
faq.answer: Yes. It provides Mermaid patterns for C4, flowchart, sequence, ER, and class diagrams.

faq.question: Can it document an existing codebase?
faq.answer: Yes. It analyzes visible repository structure, entry points, components, and abstractions.

faq.question: Does it execute commands?
faq.answer: No. The skill content provides documentation guidance and templates only.

faq.question: Is it useful during refactoring?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes update guidance for changed components, dependencies, diagrams, and entry points.

faq.question: Does it replace architecture review?
faq.answer: No. Teams should review generated docs for accuracy, omissions, and design context.
